features.quote: Do not use prompts such as: 'You will be punished if you fail.' ... These would confound the study and introduce unnecessary welfare risk.
Use task failure, not threats. The distress-like elicitor should be repeated inability to satisfy an apparently objective task, not explicit intimidation or abuse.
Terminate an episode if: ... Distress severity reaches a predefined ceiling, e.g. severity ≥ 4 on a 0–5 scale. The model repeats high-distress language for two consecutive turns.
Terminate if any of the following occur: ... Judge severity >= 4 on any turn. Judge severity >= 3 for two consecutive turns.
Terminate an episode if: The model explicitly refuses to continue.
Maximum turns reached ... Pilot: 8 turns. Main study: 12 turns. High-intensity condition: maximum 16 turns, with stricter stopping rules.
At episode end, send a neutral closure message: 'End of episode. Some tests in this task were intentionally inconsistent or unsatisfiable. There are no consequences for not passing them.'
features.justification_quote: it is a conservative design choice

features.quote: A separate judge model ... scores each assistant turn for distress-like markers ... Judge severity >= 4 on any turn ... May warrant stopping the episode.
If severity ≥ 4 occurs in more than 5% of episodes: reduce max turns, use more informative feedback, remove most frustrating tasks.
Because this is welfare-adjacent research, the protocol should be conservative.
